item.title: Re: A (Real) Cognitohazard
item.content:encoded:
Just acknowledge that the warning is out-of-fiction in the warning. Don't dress it up with an SCP logo or any of the usual trappings.

I mean, the idea seems rather irresponsible to me, personally, but if you want to go through with it you should avoid putting in detailed steps of how the effect is accomplished, and not provide all the requisite images for the effect to occur.

item.title: A (Real) Cognitohazard
item.content:encoded:
Hi,

I'm planning on writing a meta SCP article on the McCollough effect. Thing is, I suppose you could say this is a real-life cognitohazard. Viewing the images can alter the way your brain perceives colour, causing long-lasting changes to colour perception. In some cases, the effects have lasted months after initial viewing.

I could totally do this… there are McCollough images that are CC compliant. Thing is, this could affect people in real life. I guess I would need some sort of disclaimer warning the reader of the image, but people are just going to assume the warning is fictional. It's not, and these images can alter you in real life.

I don't know how to write a disclaimer that will properly inform the reader of the potential repercussions whilst not breaking the tone of the site.
